knowledge-base.overview: Jetpack Compose guardrails, composable patterns, state management, Material 3 theming, Navigation, Hilt DI, and testing for Android development. Applies to Android SDK 24+, Jetpack Compose 1.5+, Kotlin 1.9+, Material Design 3. Loaded automatically when agents work on Android .kt files using Compose.

core-principles.principle: Describe what the UI should look like; Compose handles recomposition. Never manipulate views imperatively.
State flows down from ViewModel, events flow up from composables. Always.
The framework decides when to recompose; keep composables pure and side-effect-free.
Lift state to the nearest common ancestor — prefer stateless composables that accept state as parameters.
Collect flows with collectAsStateWithLifecycle() in composables, never raw collectAsState().

guardrail.rule: Never perform side effects (network, DB, analytics) directly in a composable body. Use LaunchedEffect, DisposableEffect, or SideEffect.
Never expose MutableStateFlow or MutableState publicly from a ViewModel. Always expose an immutable StateFlow via .asStateFlow().
Collect StateFlow in composables with collectAsStateWithLifecycle(), not collectAsState(). This stops collection when the lifecycle is paused, preventing resource leaks.
guardrail.bad: val uiState by viewModel.uiState.collectAsState() // ignores lifecycle

guardrail.rule: Never construct ViewModels manually in composables. Always use hiltViewModel() for Hilt-injected ViewModels.
guardrail.bad: val vm = HomeViewModel(repository) // manual construction — bypasses Hilt scoping

guardrail.rule: Every public composable must accept modifier: Modifier = Modifier as its first optional parameter and pass it to the root layout element.
Model UI state as a sealed interface with Loading, Success, and Error subtypes. Use exhaustive when expressions to handle all states.
Subscribe to events in OnEnable, unsubscribe in OnDisable. Use DisposableEffect for cleanup-required side effects (listeners, observers).
Never pass complex objects as navigation arguments. Pass IDs only and load data from ViewModel.
Never hardcode colors, dimensions, or strings in composables. Use MaterialTheme.colorScheme.*, MaterialTheme.typography.*, and string resources.
Use remember {} for local composable state that survives recomposition; rememberSaveable when it must also survive configuration changes.
Apply @Preview to every reusable component with representative data to enable iterative development without running the app.
Provide contentDescription on all interactive and decorative icons for accessibility.
Use derivedStateOf for expensive computations derived from other state to avoid unnecessary recompositions.

project-structure.description: Standard Android project layout for Compose with Hilt, ViewModel, and Navigation.
project-structure.example: app/src/main/java/com/example/myapp/ ├── MyApplication.kt # @HiltAndroidApp ├── MainActivity.kt # @AndroidEntryPoint, setContent {} ├── navigation/ │ └── AppNavigation.kt # NavHost, route definitions (Screen sealed class) ├── ui/ │ ├── theme/ # Color.kt, Type.kt, Theme.kt │ ├── screens/ │ │ ├── home/ │ │ │ ├── HomeScreen.kt # Composable (stateless where possible) │ │ │ └── HomeViewModel.kt # ViewModel + sealed UiState │ │ └── detail/ │ │ ├── DetailScreen.kt │ │ └── DetailViewModel.kt │ └── components/ # Shared reusable composables │ ├── LoadingIndicator.kt │ └── ErrorMessage.kt ├── data/ │ ├── model/ # Domain models (@Serializable) │ ├── remote/ # Retrofit service, DTOs │ ├── local/ # Room database, DAOs │ └── repository/ # Repository implementations └── di/ # Hilt modules ├── AppModule.kt └── NetworkModule.kt

notes.note: ui/screens/: One sub-package per feature, each with Screen.kt + ViewModel.kt
ui/components/: Reusable composables shared across screens
data/: Models, repositories, API services — no Compose dependencies
di/: Hilt modules providing singletons and scoped dependencies

pattern.name: Sealed UI State + ViewModel
pattern.description: Model all UI state as a sealed interface. ViewModel exposes an immutable StateFlow; screen collects it lifecycle-aware.

navigation.description: Compose Navigation with type-safe sealed Screen routes. Pass IDs only — never complex objects.

effects.description: Use Compose side-effect APIs to manage lifecycle-aware operations.

row.trigger: On enter + when key changes (with cleanup)

row.use: Syncing Compose state to non-Compose code

theming.description: Always wrap the app root in a custom MaterialTheme composable. Support dynamic color on Android 12+.

testing.stack: JUnit4, MockK, Turbine (Flow assertions), Compose Test Rule, StandardTestDispatcher

rules.rule: Use StandardTestDispatcher + Dispatchers.setMain() for ViewModel coroutine tests
Use Turbine for StateFlow assertions (awaitItem(), cancelAndConsumeRemainingEvents())
Use MockK with coEvery/coVerify for suspend function mocking
Use createComposeRule() for isolated composable tests; query with onNodeWithText/onNodeWithTag

quick-reference.item: Pure functions, accept modifier param, no side effects in body, @Preview on every reusable component
ViewModel exposes immutable StateFlow; sealed interface for UI state; collectAsStateWithLifecycle in composables
LaunchedEffect for one-shot work, DisposableEffect for cleanup, SideEffect for Compose-to-non-Compose sync
Sealed Screen routes, pass IDs only, hiltViewModel() in composable blocks
StandardTestDispatcher + Turbine for ViewModel; createComposeRule() for UI tests
MutableStateFlow public exposure, collectAsState(), manual ViewModel construction, direct I/O in composable body
